title: Grounded Memory
summary: A local learning system that asks about unfamiliar sights and sounds, remembers evidence, and revises what it thinks it knows.
oneLiner: A local learning system that asks about unfamiliar sights and sounds, remembers evidence, and revises what it thinks it knows.

assets.label: Teaching an unfamiliar object in a synthetic video
assets.summary: The app isolates the yellow shape and asks what it is. The teacher can review an answer before saving it.

assets.label: Saved observations and learned labels
assets.summary: The recall timeline lets you revisit earlier observations. You can remove a teaching claim without deleting its source recording.

caseStudy.problem: A learner in a new environment needs to distinguish what it observed, what it inferred, and what a person taught it.
caseStudy.role: I built the Mac learning runtime and console, the paired iPhone sensing app, and the replay tools.
architecture: A Mac orders video, audio and optional pose or depth observations. A paired iPhone supplies live sensing.
Place recognition uses multiple views and recent movement. The memory stores observations, expectations, questions and revisions as separate records.
decisions: Keep source recordings and teaching claims separate so a later correction preserves the evidence.
Keep language inference on the local machine and let uncertain observations remain unresolved.
validation: Automated learning and replay checks cover place recognition, repeated observations, and corrections.
limitations: The current research build still needs end-to-end physical iPhone acceptance and recognition calibration.

cardSummary: A local learner that asks about unfamiliar sights and sounds, then revises its memory.
